title.narrative: Enhanced labour migration governance towards better protection and empowerment for Indonesian women migrant workers, domestic workers and fishers

description.narrative: Indonesia has become a significant migrant worker sending over the last four decades. The contribution of labour migration to the employment and economic conditions of Indonesia is important. Migrant workers, domestic workers, and capture fisheries workers often face significant risks in their jobs, including human rights violations, exploitation, and poor working conditions. Strengthening protections for these groups is essential to ensure they can enjoy basic rights, work under decent conditions, and are safeguarded against harmful practices. The International Labour Organization (ILO) and labour stakeholders in Indonesia recognize that all three groups are vulnerable to exploitation. They frequently endure poor working environments and are victims of human rights violations, including violence and harassment. Many find themselves trapped in cycles of forced labour and lack proper legal protection. In 2024 - 2025, ILO’s support aims at strengthening the capacity of the Government of Indonesia and its social partners to implement labour migration policies and enhancing the protection of Indonesian migrant workers, with a particular focus on the needs of women migrant workers, domestic workers, as well as migrant fishers. It will promote more inclusive protection frameworks and the empowerment of migrant workers to claim their rights throughout the migration cycle. ILO is collaborating with various stakeholders and migrant workers to ensure that rights-based and gender-responsive labour migration governance framework and protection mechanisms are mainstreamed as a part of Indonesia's post-crisis recovery agenda. Their efforts include conducting studies and assessments, providing training, offering guidance to constituents to prevent exploitation and human rights violations, and organizing public awareness campaigns. Furthermore, the ILO actively promotes reforms by engaging in public consultations and sharing information widely.
